semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Mathematical programming is a broader term that encompasses integer programming, as both deal with optimization problems subject to constraints. Though not exactly equivalent, integer programming is a type of mathematical programming.

parent_domains.justification: This domain is broader than integer programming since mixed-integer programming involves problems containing both integer and continuous variables.
Integer programming is a subset of discrete optimization, as it deals with selecting the best option from a finite set of discrete choices.
A broader domain which entails various approaches including integer programming for finding the best solution to a problem under given constraints.
This involves searching for an optimal object from a finite set of objects, and integer programming is commonly used for solving such problems.
A very broad field that includes integer programming as one of its many techniques.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Integer programming is intrinsically linked to discrete optimization as it specifically deals with optimization over discrete variables, making this the closest parent domain.

child_domains.justification: A specialized area within integer programming that focuses on linear relationships between variables while ensuring some or all variables are integers.
This can be seen as encompassing integer programming due to its nature of integrating both integer and non-integer variables, making it a child domain in some context.

closest_child_domain.justification: This is directly derived from integer programming by imposing linearity in the constraints and objective function, making it the closest child domain.

sibling_domains.justification: A sibling because they both fall under the parent domain of discrete optimization and deal with optimal selections from a finite set of options.
Both are encapsulated by broader mathematical and discrete optimization fields, without one being a subset directly of the other.
A numerical technique often used for solving optimization problems like integer programming, and both exist side by side under the broader optimization framework.
While not directly related to integer programming, algorithm design is frequently employed to develop the methods used in solving integer programming problems.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Deals with optimization where the problem space is discrete and finite, similar to integer programming, thus making it the closest sibling.

unrelated_domains.justification: This domain focuses on applying probability and statistics to programming, which is unrelated to the deterministic nature of integer programming.
While this includes integer programming, it is a broader concept and does not relate directly without considering the optimization context.
This is a process-oriented domain focused on developing algorithms, rather than being specific to integer programming.
A very broad domain that only marginally touches on integer programming.
A broader category that may include integer programming algorithms but does not specifically define a domain.
This relates to only part of what integer programming could be, not covering the full scope or being directly linked to integer programming.
It focuses on optimization with linear constraints and objective functions, not specific to the integer aspect.
A general term that includes a wide range of optimization problems, of which integer programming is just a small part.
